learner_operation: Interpret each term as a power, increment its exponent and divide by the new exponent, preserve its sign, combine the two antiderivatives and one arbitrary constant; select the equivalent expression or supply the expression before a printed + C.

fixed_features.feature: Two simple terms, unit magnitude on the nonconstant integrand coefficient, exponent != -1.
fixed_features.justification: e-371 and tutorial 701 teach sum-rule decomposition plus prerequisite power rules; tutorial 703 places general constant-factor multiplication later. Two terms preserve the observed workload; exponent -1 would require an unsupported logarithmic case.

fixed_features.feature: One constant term in normal generation; x/y/t for radio, t for derivative blank.
fixed_features.justification: Finite practice family models the three complete moderate response examples and exercises constant integration plus one power integral. Missing response/difficulty evidence for other supplied families is recorded explicitly. Variable changes are notation, not counted as mathematical diversity.

fixed_features.feature: Five math radio options or one blank before external +C.
fixed_features.justification: Observed in q-71167, q-71169 and q-133291. Correct-choice position and simplicity are not essential constraints.

answer_roles.role: Signed constant and nonconstant power to integrate
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Change magnitude/sign, polynomial exponent or reciprocal half exponent; swap order; consistently rename variable.
answer_roles.observed: All declared signs, constants -6..-1/1..6, exponents P/B 2..6 and R 3/5/7, term orders and radio variables survive deduplication.

answer_roles.role: Correct option and incorrect coefficient roles
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Shuffle positions and vary offsets, factors, and which wrong cell is omitted without creating a presentation cue.
answer_roles.observed: All five correct positions, six factors and four omitted cells observed in each radio template. Despite that coverage, all P exponent-4/6 items share a perfect coefficient-complexity cue.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Dependent answer coefficients must track changed exponents, signs and constants, while distractors must require assessing the power-rule result.
answer_roles.observed: Dependencies are mathematically correct. The grid factors force the correct coefficient to be the sole unit-numerator/one-digit-denominator candidate within its constant row for P n=4/6.

shortcut_probes.cue: Constant matching plus coefficient typography (unit numerator and one-digit denominator)
shortcut_probes.subgroup: P-grid, printed power exponent4 or6; discovery raw
shortcut_probes.strategy: For polynomial prompts with printed exponent 4 or 6: retain options whose linear coefficient matches the printed constant; choose the power fraction with numerator 1 and a one-digit denominator. Do not calculate an antiderivative of the power term.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Random choice baseline0.2; even after matching constant, guessing among two/three candidates gives1/2 or1/3. This cue instead yields certainty without the required power-rule computation. Six-factor exact domain proof, fresh samples, UI screenshots and146 accepted native cue-selected submissions corroborate it.
